title: Recording and Cre-matched shuffles gave no clear current rise-time matching in selected Allen mouse circuits
abstract: We tested whether connections with a common source or target have similar current rise times in Allen Synaptic Physiology r2.1. Shuffles kept each recording, response sign and ordered Cre-label pair fixed. The mouse source test used 202 edge pairs in 147 recordings; the target test used 196 edge pairs in 135 recordings. Both Holm-adjusted one-sided p values were 0.884. Only 62 and 65 recordings changed under the respective shuffles. Thus, this test gave no clear current rise-time matching. A secondary current-decay target association remains exploratory. This extends an earlier voltage-timing study and audits information loss under sparse matched shuffles. Selected slices, incomplete labels, fit uncertainty, exchangeability assumptions and inferred animal groups limit inference. Code, source hashes, extracted evidence, results, draws and a figure are provided.
